analysis.one_liner: Bharat Electronics is a state-owned (Navratna PSU) defence electronics company that builds radars, communication systems, electronic warfare equipment and missile/weapon systems mainly for the Indian armed forces.
analysis.whats_happening: Q2 FY27 (September quarter) results came out on 30 Oct 2026: revenue rose 26.5% YoY to ₹7,291 crore and net profit rose roughly 20% to ₹1,541 crore, but operating margin slipped to 27.85% from 29.38% a year earlier. Management followed up with an investor call on 3 Nov 2026. The bigger overhang is that FY27-to-date order inflows of about ₹7,300 crore are down 44% YoY, well short of the pace needed to hit management's own FY27 guidance of order inflows above ₹55,000 crore - largely because the ₹30,000 crore QRSAM missile-system order, pending for several quarters, is still awaiting final Cabinet Committee on Security approval.
analysis.plain_terms: BEL makes electronics for India's army, navy and air force - radars, communication gear, and missile systems - almost all of it sold to the government. This quarter's profit and revenue both grew at a healthy clip, but the company earned a slightly smaller slice of profit from every rupee of sales than a year ago. The tension to watch: BEL's share price has partly priced in a very large missile-system order (QRSAM) that is still stuck waiting for a government committee's sign-off, so new orders are coming in much slower than the company's own full-year target implies.
analysis.quarters: Revenue +26.5% YoY to ₹7,291 crore and net profit +19.8% YoY to ₹1,541 crore in Q2 FY27, with EBITDA up 20% to ₹2,041 crore. Operating margin contracted to 27.85% from 29.38% a year ago - so this quarter's growth was volume-led rather than margin-led, and the margin trend moved the wrong way even as sales grew. H1 FY27 net profit is ₹2,595 crore versus ₹2,258 crore in H1 FY26, up 15%. Management has reiterated FY27 guidance of ~15% revenue growth and a 28% EBITDA margin, alongside order inflows exceeding ₹55,000 crore - a target now at risk given YTD inflows of only ~₹7,300 crore (down 44% YoY). No non-comparable accounting items were flagged by the company.
analysis.performance_read: The stock is down 20.9% from its 6 March 2026 peak of ₹467.81 to ₹369.9. This is not a corporate-action artifact - BEL's last stock split was in September 2022, more than four years before this peak, so there is no bonus/split distortion in the chart; it is a genuine price pullback. Longer-term returns remain strong: +184% over 3 years and +488% over 5 years, far ahead of the Nifty (+21% and +29% respectively). However, defence peer HAL has done better over 5 years (+694% vs BEL's +488%) and has also outperformed BEL over the last year and 3 months, during which BEL fell while HAL rose - a relative underperformance worth noting.
analysis.valuation_read: P/E sits roughly in the 44-48x range depending on source, and P/B is about 11.2x against a peer median near 13.5x. That is rich for a company guiding to ~15% revenue growth. It is expensive mainly because the market is pricing in the pending ₹30,000 crore QRSAM order and India's broader domestic-defence-manufacturing push, not because current-year earnings growth alone justifies the multiple. Whether that premium is warranted hinges entirely on if and when QRSAM converts into a signed contract - a separate question from whether the stock looks cheap today (it does not, by standard multiples).
analysis.growth_read: Growth this quarter was volume-led: revenue rose 26.5% but operating margin fell from 29.38% to 27.85%, meaning more sales came at a lower profit rate per rupee. That is a less durable growth pattern than one where margin holds or expands alongside volume. Management's FY27 guidance (15% revenue growth, 28% margin) implies some margin recovery is expected through the rest of the year.
analysis.health_read: BEL is debt-free (debt-to-equity of 0) with ROCE around 37% and ROE in the mid-20s to high-20s depending on source - a strong, low-financial-risk balance sheet. The real risk here is business/execution risk, not financial risk: order inflows are running well behind the company's own full-year target, and a large chunk of future growth depends on a single pending government approval (QRSAM). Cash conversion (operating cash flow versus reported profit) was not verified in this review - check on Screener, as PSU defence contractors often carry elevated receivables tied to government billing cycles.
analysis.ownership_read: The promoter is the President of India (Government of India) holding 51.14% - as a sovereign promoter, pledging is not applicable and none is reported. Domestic institutions (including mutual funds at ~14.9%) hold a combined ~21.9%, while foreign institutional ownership is light at just 2.08%, and public holding is 8.65%. No well-known individual investor shows up on the register for this stock.
strengths: Debt-free balance sheet with ROCE near 37%, among the highest in Indian capital goods/defence
H1 FY27 net profit up 15% YoY to ₹2,595 crore on revenue growth of ~26% in Q2
Order book of ₹68,717 crore (as of 1 Oct 2026) gives multi-year revenue visibility, roughly 2.3x trailing annual revenue
Zero promoter pledge, with sovereign (Government of India) promoter backing
watchpoints: FY27-to-date order inflows of ~₹7,300 crore are down 44% YoY, well behind the >₹55,000 crore full-year guidance
Operating margin contracted to 27.85% from 29.38% YoY even as revenue grew - growth is volume-led, not margin-led
₹30,000 crore QRSAM order has been pending Cabinet Committee on Security approval for several quarters with no firm signing date
Stock already down 20.9% from its March 2026 peak and underperforming peer HAL over the last year and 3 months
analysis.one_thing: Whether and when the ₹30,000 crore QRSAM missile-system order clears Cabinet Committee on Security approval and converts into a signed contract - this single event determines if FY27 order-inflow guidance of over ₹55,000 crore is achievable and whether the order book can cross ₹1 lakh crore.
analysis.data_notes: Q2 FY27 results cross-checked across multiple financial news sources (Upstox, Kotak Neo, business-news aggregators) and consistent on revenue/PAT figures. Shareholding data from Trendlyne/AngelOne-style aggregators as of September 2026. Valuation ratios vary by source and date - P/E ranges from 43.89x to ~48x and ROE from 24.37% to 27.88%; both ranges are reported here rather than averaged. Operating cash flow/cash-conversion data and the next dividend record date were not verified - check on Screener.
